newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA TO CANCEL GAS PIPELINE CONCESSIONS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA TO CANCEL GAS PIPELINE CONCESSIONS.

text.p: Bulgaria will cancel two pipeline concessions for transiting Russian gas announced by the previous government as they violate the concession law, Bulgaria's new deputy prime minister said on Monday.
Alexander Bozhkov told reporters Bulgarian and Russian experts would start work on finding an alternative scheme, which would enable construction work to go ahead.

"We will stop the concession procedure because it is incorrect legally. This is the opinion of the Russian and the Bulgarian side. We are giving up the concession as it is because it can not be realised as it is," Bozhkov said.
Bozhkov was speaking after talks with a Russian delegation headed by Deputy Prime Minister Oleg Lobov, which arrived on Monday. The delegation includes Gazprom president Rem Vyahirev.
"All our legal consultations show that the whole procedure breaches the concession law and in this case we should seek a working scheme," Bozhkov told reporters.

Bulgaria's former Socialist government on February 7 invited bidders for one concession on the existing pipelines and for transiting Russian natural gas through them, and for a second concession for pipelines planned to be built and for transiting Russian gas through them.
Bozhkov said that immediately after the meeting of the two delegations, Bulgarian and Russian experts would start work on finding an alternative scheme.
"With or without a concession a decision should be taken, a decision which is long-lasting...and will allow the start of the pipelines' construction in Bulgaria in a very short term," Bozhkov said.
"Whether it will be a concession or a bilateral or triangular contract, will be decided at the experts level."

Gazprom holds 50 percent in a joint stock company, Topenergy, which was set up in Bulgaria in 1995 together with Bulgaria's Bulgargas, which has 25.1 percent. The remaining 24.9 percent are distributed among Bulgarian banks and firms.
Last year Topenergy asked for a concession for transiting pipelines. The company needs to increase the Bulgarian distribution system from 17 billion cubic metres to some 29 billion cubic metres.

An enlargement of the network will be needed because gas supplies to Turkey will be increased and the project envisages gas supplies to Greece, Macedonia, Serbia and possibly Albania in the future, Topenergy officials say.
Bulgaria has a gas network of some 2,000 km, including links to Turkey, Greece and Macedonia and plans to construct a new link to Serbia.
